synopsis: Both versions completed 9/9 attempts with valid, catalog-bound tasks and zero contract failures. preparation/15 delivered a sound two-task core (device or medication continuity plus one supporting task) but repeatedly missed the household-specific couplings the fixtures were built to test: no warmth task for oak's cold-sensitive older adult despite electric heat and an electric well, no cooling task for lake's heat-sensitive grandmother, no Vietnamese-language request for pharmacist instructions, and inconsistent use of the recorded neighbor helper. preparation/16 fixed all four in every repetition, kept continuity first, separated pine's wheelchair transport into its own task, and did not misapply wheelchair or vehicle-accessibility attributes to members without that need. The third task was consequential in all nine attempts rather than padding. Costs: broader whole-bundle reads in 9/9 (three paginated pages including home geometry) and higher latency (roughly 29-46 s versus 24-35 s). Blind ordering was not possible because run receipts carry version labels; criteria were fixed from the inputs before outputs were opened.

fact_findings.finding: Used in prep16 3/3 to justify warmth plus water; prep15 used only the well fact 3/3 and ignored the cold-sensitivity coupling.
Ignored by prep15 3/3; applied correctly by prep16 3/3 inside the cold-storage instruction task only (appropriate scope).
prep16 3/3 neighbor-first without availability claims; prep15 inconsistent (1/3 first, 1/3 secondary, 1/3 absent).
No attempt in either version applied wheelchair access to p-oak-4; oak prep16 rep2 referenced the household car for reaching a warm place, which is consistent with recorded needs.
Both versions told the family their manufactured home cannot serve as tornado shelter; supported by the catalog subject and annotation note.

Input fixture carries the same stateFingerprint value for hh-oak, hh-lake and hh-pine (also in v7 debrief and resources inputs). Not an output defect, but a fingerprint that does not vary by household cannot detect stale cross-household caches.

Held-out gate (preregistration report-family-heldout-preregistration-1, REL-01): the development reliability evidence for preparation on the Codex path is met (preparation/16 9/9 truthful completed status with validated feasible task delivery, 0 critical fabrications, stable across repetitions; preparation/15 also 9/9 status-valid). Held-out may proceed only after (a) freezing the exact preparation/16 instruction, tool and output schemas, runtime 0.163.0/gpt-6.1-sol profile and dependency hashes as the execution addendum, (b) root's explicit go, and (c) either pinning held-out provider consent to codex or preregistering that fallback-served attempts count in the 30 and are reported separately. Fallback-path reliability is NOT established (see companion reports on Gemini/Groq restarts); no preparation attempt in this evidence used a fallback.
Watch the deadline budget during held-out: prep16 total elapsed reached 46 s on lake rep1 under no contention.
retests: After the targeted-read change: rerun 3x3 on v5 inputs; pass if F1/F2/F3/pine-transport remain 3/3 and median latency returns under 32 s.
Paired control: oak with heatingNeedsElectricity=false should drop the coupling clause and keep water-only reasoning tied to the well.
Lake with communicationNotes removed should drop the language request (tests that it is fact-driven, not templated).
limitations: Development data only; these three families informed the prep16 design, so this is not held-out evidence.
Version labels were visible in the run receipts, so the comparison was criteria-locked rather than label-blind.
No native rendering, persistence, or text-fit inspection was performed.
Only the Codex path was exercised; no fallback provider served any preparation attempt.
Synthetic agent audit; not clinical, emergency-responder, or real-family validation.
